description: Language-oriented scanner profiles. Unicode encodes scripts/characters, not languages; these profiles map requested source-language research categories to their principal Unicode script ranges.

profiles.notes: Hieroglyphic source text. Unicode U+13000-U+1342F is Egyptian Hieroglyphs; U+13460-U+143FF is Egyptian Hieroglyphs Extended-A. Hieratic/Demotic are not assumed to be represented by these hieroglyph blocks.
Han ranges cover common and extension ideographs. Chinese language identification remains contextual because Han is shared with Japanese Kanji and other East Asian writing systems.
Japanese commonly mixes Hiragana, Katakana, and Han/Kanji; Latin and punctuation may also occur.
The Greek Extended block is important for polytonic and scholarly Ancient Greek text.
Latin is a script as well as the language family label used by the requested source-language scanner. Classical Latin input can contain basic Latin plus extended scholarly characters.
